Evidence for Evolution
¨Biochemical Evidence
¤All living organisms:
   nUse the same basic biochemical molecules
   nUtilize same DNA triplet code
   nUtilize same 20 amino acids in their proteins
¤DNA base-sequence differences:
   nWhen very similar, suggest recent common descent
   nWhen more different, suggest more ancient common descent
explanation: Biochemical evidence demonstrates the unity of life through shared molecular machinery. All living organisms utilize the same basic biochemical molecules, the same DNA triplet genetic code, and the same 20 amino acids to synthesize proteins. By comparing DNA base sequences, scientists can infer evolutionary relationships: highly similar DNA sequences suggest a recent common ancestor (recent common descent), whereas greater sequence differences suggest a more distant common ancestor (ancient common descent).

questions.q: Which biochemical characteristic is shared by all living organisms on Earth?
opts: They all possess a postanal tail as adults.
They utilize the same DNA triplet code and 20 amino acids in their proteins.
They contain identical DNA base sequences.
They undergo the same geographical migrations.
questions.exp: According to the notes, all living organisms share basic biochemical molecules, use the same DNA triplet code, and use the same 20 amino acids for protein synthesis.

questions.q: What do minor differences in DNA base sequences between two species indicate?
questions.exp: The notes explain that DNA base-sequence differences suggest recent common descent when they are very similar, and more ancient common descent when they are more different.
